subtype: Stage 6: Rebuilt at a different depth or ended [Response]
passage:
A year after the whole thing, Rania and Jin still worked on the same floor of the design studio in Toronto. On Friday Jin stopped by her desk with two coffees, the way he used to, and asked about her weekend.
"Went hiking with my sister," Rania said. "It was good." She didn't mention the flat she was trying to buy, or her worries about her mother's visa. Those went to Leila now, and to her sister.
They laughed about a client's font choices. It was pleasant. It was real, even. Jin had corrected what he'd said about her to the director and never repeated anything since.
But Rania had learned something about who holds what. Jin was good for coffee, for design talk, for a laugh on a slow afternoon. Not for the things that could be used.
When he left, she found she wasn't bitter. Just clear.

qa.q: What did Rania tell Jin she did at the weekend?
qa.a: Rania said she went hiking with her sister.

qa.q: How does Rania feel about Jin now, and what shows it?
qa.a: Rania feels calm and clear rather than bitter; she enjoys the chat but keeps her personal worries for Leila and her sister. 🙂

qa.q: What limits has Rania set, and why do they work?
qa.a: Rania shares light things like work and weekends with Jin but nothing that could be used against her, so the friendship stays cordial without risking another hurt.

qa.q: How might Jin experience the friendship now?
qa.a: Jin may notice Rania is warm but more guarded, and understand that the old depth was the cost of what he did.

grounding: Shows a friendship rebuilt as cordial and careful, with clear limits on what is shared, after a betrayal was corrected.

The staffroom at St. Anne's emptied fast after the last bell. Devika packed her marking into her bag while Wasim hovered by the kettle.
"Coffee on Saturday? Like old times?" he asked.
It had been eight months since he told the principal about her private complaint. He'd apologised, a quick "sorry if you were hurt", and then, three weeks ago, she'd heard he had passed on something about Mrs Joseph too.
Devika zipped the bag. "I don't think so, Wasim. I'm glad for the years we had. But I'm not going to keep being close."
He looked stung. "Because of one thing?"
"Because it wasn't one thing." She said it gently. She wasn't angry any more; she'd done that part in the winter.
On the way out she stopped at the library to return a book to Ms Pinto, who had become the person she called on hard days. It felt like choosing well.

qa.q: How long had it been since Wasim told the principal about Devika's complaint?
qa.a: It had been eight months since he told the principal about her private complaint.

qa.q: Why did Devika say no to coffee, and how did she feel saying it?
qa.a: Devika saw the pattern had repeated with Mrs Joseph, so she ended the closeness; she felt calm and gentle, no longer angry.

qa.q: What makes Devika's ending a healthy one?
qa.a: Devika is honest but kind, thanks Wasim for the good years, and turns to a safer friend like Ms Pinto instead of seeking revenge.

qa.q: Why might Wasim react with 'Because of one thing?'
qa.a: Wasim seems to see his betrayal as a single slip, while Devika sees a pattern; he may feel stung and not yet understand why the trust has gone.

grounding: Illustrates a woman ending a friendship without bitterness after a repeated betrayal, having learned whom she can trust with what.
